author: Codex paired assessor

source_artifacts.claim: Special Delivery source defines the heavy parcel, WEIGH/STEADY/RESCUE pads and their doors/stabilization effects, the unstable packing bridge over slime, collectibles and matching exits.
The shared bridge helper sets collapseAfter to 0.8 seconds and resetAfter to 2 seconds.
A heavy crate moves only when two connected player pushers provide the same direction.
Players count as one weight each; a heavy crate contributes two to an any-accepting pad; hold pads release while latch pads remain active.
An unsteady occupied bridge collapses after its configured interval and returns after its reset interval.
Hazard overlap marks the state dead; both actors must overlap their own exit for completion.
A death resets the room from its authored start after a short delay; the replay path must repeat the crate/pad setup.
Earlier level_09 authors the heavy nutrient cargo, team-push language, TEAM pad with minimum weight two, and gated crossing.
Earlier level_04 authors Pac STEADY stabilizing a bridge and opening Isp’s crossing, followed by Isp latching RESCUE to maintain the bridge and open Pac’s route.

prior_knowledge.concept: Two heroes must push a heavy parcel together; team lifting/pushing and a two-weight TEAM pad were introduced at level_09.

evidence.claim: Level_09 source explicitly says both push the heavy nutrient sac onto TEAM and defines a heavy box plus a minWeight-two team pad.
The earlier screenshot visibly says Team lift / Team shove and shows a TEAM box beside ANY TEAM x2.

prior_knowledge.concept: Pac holds a STEADY pad to stabilize a dangerous bridge and open Isp’s crossing; Isp then latches RESCUE to keep the bridge stable and open Pac’s route. This exact role order was introduced at level_04.

evidence.claim: Level_04 source names Pac’s STEADY hold, Isp’s bridge crossing and RESCUE latch, with an unstable bridge and lethal slime below.
The earlier screenshot shows PAC STEADY and ISP RESCUE STAYS ON over an unstable bridge/slime gap.

prior_knowledge.concept: The current level combines the prior heavy-push/weigh and Pac-steady/Isp-rescue sequences by staging them as one delivery route; this integration is new.

evidence.claim: The authored hint chains heavy-parcel WEIGH, Pac STEADY, Isp crossing and RESCUE in one room, adding load gate/dispatch dependencies.

mechanics.fact: The heavy nutrient sac starts at x220; it requires two connected heroes pushing in one direction. When it sits on the any-accepting WEIGH pad, its weight of two activates the hold pad and opens the loading gate.

evidence.claim: WEIGH has minWeight 2 and opens loading_gate; the crate at x220 is heavy.
A heavy crate requires at least two connected pushers.
An any pad counts a heavy crate as weight 2, sufficient for the pad threshold.

mechanics.fact: Pac must stand on the Pac-only STEADY hold pad. It stabilizes the packing bridge and opens the ISP-only bridge gate while Pac remains there. Isp crosses to RESCUE and latches it; that permanently stabilizes the bridge for this run and opens loading_gate, isp_bridge and pac_dispatch.

evidence.claim: STEADY stabilizes packing_bridge and opens isp_bridge; RESCUE is an Isp-only latch that stabilizes the bridge and opens the remaining gates.
Hold occupancy activates effects while latched pads remain active after occupancy ends.

mechanics.fact: The packing bridge is unstable when not stabilized: it collapses after 0.8 seconds of occupied instability and resets after 2 seconds. Packing slime directly underneath is lethal on overlap; keeping STEADY held until RESCUE latches provides the safe route.

evidence.claim: The packing bridge helper defines the 0.8-second collapse and 2-second reset intervals.
The unstable bridge spans x600-880 and the slime hazard occupies the area below it.
Overlap with an active harmful hazard sets state status to dead.

mechanics.fact: Both actors must overlap their matching separate exits. The crate can remain on WEIGH until the RESCUE latch opens loading_gate; after rescue, Pac can leave STEADY and follow the bridge to the dispatch exit. Isp’s exit is at x990 and Pac’s at x1050.

evidence.claim: The route-defining gates and distinct exits are authored; the hint specifies the ordered role transfer.
Completion requires both actors to overlap their own exit.

mechanics.fact: The two collectibles are optional: an Isp blue collectible on the packing bridge at x745 and a Pac orange one beside the STEADY area at x540.

evidence.claim: The two collectibles are owner-specific and lie away from the required pad/exit conditions.

legal_routes.name: Two-person WEIGH, Pac holds STEADY, Isp latches RESCUE, both reach exits

steps.goal: Open the loading route with the heavy delivery.
steps.action: Approach the heavy nutrient sac from the left and push together until it rests on WEIGH; leave it on the pad to keep the loading gate open.
steps.expected_feedback: The heavy crate counts as two weights and activates WEIGH; the gate opens.

evidence.claim: The source route hint and definition specify a jointly pushed heavy crate on a two-weight hold pad.
Two connected pushers are necessary to move the heavy crate.
The heavy crate contributes weight two and the hold pad activates at its threshold.

steps.goal: Keep the bridge safe and open Isp’s crossing.
steps.action: Move to and remain on the Pac-only STEADY pad while Isp crosses the packing bridge.
steps.expected_feedback: The bridge is stabilized and the Isp bridge gate opens while Pac remains on STEADY.

evidence.claim: STEADY is Pac-only, hold-activated, and stabilizes the bridge while opening the Isp crossing.

steps.goal: Secure the bridge/dispatch route for both heroes.
steps.action: Cross the stabilized bridge and stand on Isp-only RESCUE to latch it.
steps.expected_feedback: RESCUE stays active, stabilizes the bridge, opens the loading gate/ISP crossing/Pac dispatch gate.

evidence.claim: RESCUE is Isp-only and latched; its effects stabilize the bridge and open all remaining gates.

steps.action: With RESCUE latched, leave the WEIGH/STEADY area, cross to dispatch and stop at each actor’s own exit rather than continuing past it.
steps.expected_feedback: Both actors overlap their respective exits and the level completes.

evidence.claim: The rescue latch opens the dispatch path and source defines two distinct exits.
Both matching exit overlaps are required for completion.
The optional source hint names the mandatory causal order; the pad/gate/bridge/exit definitions support it.

evidence.locator: text:For room 15, the final Isp box is at `(1070, 464)` while its exit is at `(990, 440, 42, 60)`. Pac overlaps its exit.
evidence.claim: The retained source-bound native trace confirms a meaningful endpoint correction is needed for Isp; the route itself remains partial.

isp: Works with Pac to push the heavy parcel onto WEIGH.
After Pac holds STEADY, crosses the stabilized bridge and latches RESCUE; then reaches Isp’s x990 exit and must stop within that distinct exit.
pac: Works with Isp to push the heavy parcel to WEIGH, then holds STEADY so the bridge remains stable and opens Isp’s crossing.
After Isp latches RESCUE, leaves the pad and reaches Pac’s x1050 dispatch exit.

common_mistakes.mistake: Pac leaves STEADY before Isp has latched RESCUE, while Isp is still on the unstable bridge.
common_mistakes.consequence: The occupied bridge loses stabilization; after 0.8 seconds it collapses and Isp can fall into the lethal packing slime. This is a source-inferred likely failure, not a failure observed in the retained route.
common_mistakes.recovery: If the fall kills Isp, the runtime automatically rebuilds the room after a short death delay. The team must repeat the heavy-parcel push and role sequence; the route evidence contains no specific bridge-collapse retry, so human recovery cost remains unmeasured.

evidence.claim: STEADY is a hold; RESCUE is a latch; the occupied bridge lies above packing_slime.
An unsteady occupied bridge collapses after 0.8 seconds.
An overlap with active packing slime is lethal.
Death returns the room to its authored start after a short delay, requiring the initial sequence to be replayed.

common_mistakes.mistake: The team carries through to the far-right side and Isp continues past his own exit.
common_mistakes.consequence: In the corrected native replay of the retained route, Pac overlaps his exit but Isp ends at x1070, beyond his x990 exit; the room remains playing, both actors alive. The earlier browser campaign likewise needed an additional Pac jump and Isp movement back toward his distinct exit before completion.
common_mistakes.recovery: This sampled endpoint is a harmless reversal: after Pac jumps clear, steer Isp left into the Isp exit. The historical browser campaign completed after that ordinary-input adaptation; do not treat the original partial trace alone as a completion or a defect.

evidence.claim: The exact retained native trace ends in playing rather than complete.
Isp does not overlap his own exit at the trace endpoint.
Pac does overlap his own exit in the same partial trace.

evidence.locator: text:The later complete state belongs to that adapted run, not to the route alone.
evidence.claim: The historical browser completion followed an ordinary-input adaptation; it was not the retained route alone.
The older browser record names the Pac jump and Isp return-to-exit as the room15 adaptation.
The historical campaign records completion only after the adapted input sequence.

optional_collectibles: Optional Isp blue collectible on the bridge at x745; optional Pac orange collectible near STEADY at x540. Neither collectible is required for opening gates or reaching both exits.

reasoning.rationale: There are several linked dependencies: a heavy crate must sit on a weight-two pad; Pac then holds STEADY to stabilize a bridge and open Isp’s gate; Isp must latch RESCUE before Pac can leave STEADY safely and before both can use dispatch. The visible labels name each task but not the full order.

evidence.claim: The authored hint and effect graph create a multi-stage WEIGH → STEADY → RESCUE dependency chain.
The heavy crate adds an actual two-person push requirement.

cooperation.rationale: The heavy parcel requires both players pushing together, followed by distinct Pac-hold and Isp-cross/latch roles. The roles hand off after the latch so Pac can cross; this is more than one simple handoff, though no continuous simultaneous precision is required.

evidence.claim: A heavy crate requires two connected pushers.
Pac-only STEADY and Isp-only RESCUE form the later role handoff.

execution.rationale: The route involves a cooperative crate placement, walking onto two specific pads, crossing a flat bridge, and stopping within separate exit zones. The authored path needs no sequence of precision jumps; one historical endpoint does overshoot Isp’s exit and needs a simple left correction.

evidence.claim: The route is floor/flat bridge movement between pads and nearby exits.

evidence.locator: text:For room 15, the final Isp box is at `(1070, 464)` while its exit is at `(990, 440, 42, 60)`.
evidence.claim: A retained route overshoots the distinct Isp exit but not through a hazardous maneuver.

timing.rationale: The safe route has no timed window while Pac keeps STEADY held; Isp may cross at a normal pace and RESCUE remains latched. Timing matters only if Pac releases before Isp reaches RESCUE, which is a sequencing risk rather than a narrow required window.

evidence.claim: STEADY can stay held until Isp reaches the latch pad; RESCUE then latches.
Hold effects persist while occupied and a latch stays active after release.

hazards.rationale: The mandatory bridge crosses over a lethal slime strip and can collapse if left unstabilized; Pac’s STEADY and Isp’s RESCUE create a visible safe route. This is a real exposure with a readable safe approach, not repeated scarce-refuge exposure.

evidence.claim: The packing bridge spans the slime hazard and is unstable until stabilized.
The bridge collapses after 0.8 seconds if occupied while not stabilized.
Slime overlap marks the room dead.

novelty.rationale: A two-person heavy push/weight pad was already taught at level_09, and Pac STEADY with Isp’s RESCUE latch across an unstable bridge was taught at level_04. This room recombines those known patterns around a heavy delivery and a new load-gate-to-dispatch order, rather than introducing unfamiliar physics.

evidence.claim: Team lift/shove and ANY TEAM x2 appeared earlier.
PAC STEADY and ISP RESCUE STAYS ON were visibly introduced earlier.
The current source combines both prior pad patterns with a new crate/dispatch dependency.

recovery_cost.rationale: An early STEADY release while Isp is on the bridge can collapse the bridge into slime; source says that is lethal and runtime returns both to the start, so the heavy two-person push and pad sequence must be repeated. This material cost is source-inferred, not witnessed in an actual failed route. By contrast, the retained trace’s exit overrun is a small no-death reversal.

evidence.claim: The bridge collapses on the unsafe occupied interval.
Slime is lethal.
Death resets the whole level after a brief delay.

evidence.locator: text:The route ends with both players still alive and no phase transition
evidence.claim: The observed exit overrun was not a lethal failure and should not be confused with bridge-mistake recovery.

solution_clarity.rationale: The visible “Weigh it first,” TEAM/WEIGH 2x2 labels, PAC STEADY and ISP RESCUE STAYS ON identify the relevant objects and roles. However, the idle frame does not explain that the heavy parcel itself counts as two, that Pac must keep the bridge held only until Isp latches RESCUE, or that the Isp exit is distinct and left of Pac’s. The optional hint is excluded from base clarity.

evidence.claim: The current screenshot makes WEIGH 2x2, TEAM parcel, Pac STEADY, Isp RESCUE STAYS ON, hazard gap and exits visible.
Source contains causal weight and pad rules absent from the idle screenshot; the optional hint states the order.

control_friction.rationale: Historical ordinary-input browser actions and a current-native replay do not measure current shared-keyboard event reliability or comfort for two humans. Separate key clusters are listed, but friction remains unknown.

evidence.claim: The idle packet lists WASD and arrow-key controls but contains no input events.
Route evidence cannot establish two-human keyboard comfort.

confidence_reason: Source resolves the causal route, load threshold, bridge danger and pad transfer. A current-native replay confirms the retained trace’s partial state, and a historical browser run completed only after an ordinary-input exit correction. The source route is coherent, but no current full route replay or failed bridge-recovery case was retained; the fatal mistake and its reset cost are source-inferred, not human measurements.

confirmed: The visible TEAM delivery and WEIGH 2x2 label correctly suggested a shared-load task; level_09 already exposed team-pushing/heavy cargo language and a weight-two pad.
The visible PAC STEADY and ISP RESCUE STAYS ON labels correctly suggested separate bridge roles; level_04 introduced Pac stabilizing an unstable bridge and Isp latching RESCUE.
Idle dialogue changes were not treated as action feedback; no first-pass action is reclassified as observed after source review.
missed_mechanics: The parcel is a heavy crate requiring two simultaneous connected pushers, and the heavy crate alone supplies the WEIGH pad’s weight-two threshold.

WEIGH opens the loading gate while Pac moves to STEADY; Pac must hold it as Isp crosses the unstable bridge and latches RESCUE. That latch stabilizes the bridge and opens the remaining gates so Pac can cross and both can reach exits.
The bridge spans lethal slime and collapses after 0.8 seconds if an occupied bridge loses stabilization; the intended safe transfer is Pac’s hold until Isp’s latch.
The two collectibles are owner-specific and optional; neither affects the mandatory gate/exit sequence.
incorrect_inferences: No first-pass hypothesis was stated as a confirmed mechanic, so there is no committed false claim to correct. It left open whether the TEAM block, both heroes, or another load activates WEIGH; source resolves that by distinguishing two-person pushing from the heavy crate’s weight-two activation.
changed_judgments: Reasoning moved from 2 to 3 because the route is a chain of load activation, safe bridge opening, a timed handoff between hold and latch, and final distinct exits, rather than only a weight-pad hypothesis.
Cooperation moved from 2 to 3 because the heavy crate needs both pushers at once and the bridge route then requires different Pac-hold and Isp-latch roles.
Execution moved from unknown to 2: the mandatory path is mostly push-and-walk with careful pad and exit placement, not a repeated precision-jump sequence.
Timing moved from unknown to 1: with STEADY properly held there is no deadline; the bridge’s collapse interval punishes premature release but does not create a required narrow timing window.
Hazards moved from unknown to 2 because the unstable bridge sits over lethal slime, yet the visible STEADY/RESCUE safe approach controls exposure.
Novelty remains 2: source confirms the prior room introductions and shows a recombination of the same heavy-team-load and steady/rescue bridge patterns.

Recovery changed from unknown to 3 because source mechanics show that releasing STEADY while Isp is on the bridge can kill and reset the whole room, making the heavy push and pad chain repeat. This is source-inferred and not a recorded failed retry; the observed exit overrun instead needs only a small reversal.
Solution clarity remains 2: visible labels identify objects and likely roles but leave the two-weight crate rule and exact hold-to-latch transfer to infer.
unresolved: The corrected 1,072-tick native replay of the retained room15 route remains playing: Pac overlaps his exit, but Isp is at x1070 beyond the x990 exit. This is a partial trace, not evidence the room cannot be completed.
A separate historical browser campaign completed room15 only after a Pac jump and Isp return toward his own exit; that older adapted completion is not a current full route replay.
No retained failure tests premature STEADY release, the resulting slime death, or the full retry burden; these consequences are source inference only.
Whether new pairs infer that WEIGH must be stabilized by the parked heavy parcel while Pac leaves for STEADY, then hold through Isp’s RESCUE, remains unknown.
Current two-human shared-keyboard friction and novice route timing are not measured.

single_operator_note: One operator must coordinate both directional inputs to move the heavy parcel, then hold Pac at STEADY while steering Isp across the bridge, then switch to Pac and Isp exit correction. The distinct key clusters permit simultaneous keys, but attention switching and the deliberate hold/latch order may be harder for one operator; this is not part of the two-human baseline or measured.
